chapter: Apollo years, Eubie Blake and failing eyesight
title: Moving to the Apollo and introducing Ella to Chick Webb
summary: Whaley recalls the Apollo's productive era, amateur night, and repeats how he introduced Ella Fitzgerald to Chick Webb.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: We were talking about the Apollo Theatre, see, I went there from the Lafayette into the Opera House in '30 and went into the Apollo Theatre, I think it's in '31. Now, all the big bands came in there and that was an era of productivity, oh, they were beautiful see, all new bands would come along and we had -- I remember Ralph Cooper was MC'ing, Willie Bryant was MC, another guy was there, he played golf.
Well, anyway, we used to have an amateur hour, I told
Say it again. I'd like to hear it.

We used to have amateur hour and all these kids would come in and you know, sign up for the amateur night, Wednesday night was the amateur night and Ella used to over to Brooklyn and win all the prizes so she came over today and I said listen, come by here Thursday afternoon and I'll introduce you to a bandleader, that was Chick Webb and I says, he'll do something for you, because he's got a coming band and he works all around.
Chick Webb was a drummer, sort of a hunchback fellow, wasn't he.

Yeah, that's it, little Chick, so he played up at the Savoy. So sure enough Ella came in and I introduced her to Chick and his wife and I told her all you got to do is get her some clothes, get her a dress and have her hair fixed and she'd do the rest, so sure enough, Ella Fitzgerald come on and I used to tell everybody, well, I'm the one that give her a quarter to go out and get some coffee and hang out and wait around. I says I'm the one that discovered her, but Chick Webb was the one who developed her. Because he had a band so she could work.
That's beautiful. Because you were a musical director at the Apollo Theatre.
Yeah, I was musical director there.
